items.question: A man and a woman are discussing package holidays.

script.speaker: man
script.text: We're thinking of booking a package holiday this year. I know you prefer organising everything yourself.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: I do. I like finding little restaurants and guest houses that aren't in any guidebook.

script.speaker: man
script.text: That's fine for you, but I find planning stressful. With a package, someone else deals with the flights and the transfers.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Fair enough, though you pay for that convenience. It usually costs more than booking separately.

script.speaker: man
script.text: Not always. Last year we got a week by the sea for less than the flights alone would have cost.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Really? I used to assume packages were always expensive. I'm still doubtful, though.

script.speaker: man
script.text: Check the prices. The downside is that you're stuck with the hotel, and the beach is crowded in August.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: That's my main objection too. I'd hate to spend the whole week among crowds of people.

script.speaker: man
script.text: So why not go in June? It's cheaper and much quieter.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Good idea. I'd want to avoid the school holidays anyway.

statements.text: Planning a trip on your own lets you find places that tourists rarely visit.

explanation.en: The woman likes finding restaurants and guest houses that aren't in any guidebook. The man never says this.
explanation.es: A la mujer le gusta encontrar restaurantes y pensiones que no salen en las guías. El hombre no lo dice.

statements.text: Organising everything yourself can be a source of stress.

explanation.en: The man says "I find planning stressful". The woman enjoys organising.
explanation.es: El hombre dice "I find planning stressful". A la mujer le gusta organizar.

statements.text: A package holiday can actually be cheaper than separate bookings.

explanation.en: The man gives an example from last year. The woman says she is still doubtful.
explanation.es: El hombre da un ejemplo del año pasado. La mujer dice que aún tiene dudas.

statements.text: Busy beaches in the peak season spoil a holiday.

explanation.en: The man says the beach is crowded in August, and the woman says "That's my main objection too" about the crowds.
explanation.es: El hombre dice que la playa está llena en agosto y la mujer dice "That's my main objection too" sobre las multitudes.

items.question: A man and a woman are discussing going to the cinema.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: We went to the cinema on Saturday, and I'd forgotten how different it feels from watching at home.

script.speaker: man
script.text: Different how? I can't remember the last time I went. The screen at home is big enough, and I can pause whenever I like.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Pausing is precisely the problem. At home I'm always checking my phone, but in a dark room with strangers you're completely absorbed.

script.speaker: man
script.text: I'll give you that. At home I'm half watching and half scrolling too. But tickets are so expensive now that it's hard to justify going.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Maybe, but you can find cheaper tickets on weekday afternoons.

script.speaker: man
script.text: Even so, I wonder if cinemas will survive, except for the big blockbusters.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: I'm more optimistic. People still want to go out and share an experience. Look at how many small independent cinemas have reopened.

script.speaker: man
script.text: I hadn't thought of it that way. I used to believe they were finished.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: They'll change, certainly. Perhaps with live music or talks before the films.

script.speaker: man
script.text: That would tempt me, I must admit.

statements.text: It is hard to give a film your full attention at home.

explanation.en: The woman says she is always checking her phone at home, and the man admits he is "half watching and half scrolling".
explanation.es: La mujer dice que en casa siempre mira el móvil y el hombre admite que está "half watching and half scrolling".

statements.text: The price of tickets makes going to the cinema difficult to justify.

explanation.en: The man says tickets are so expensive it's hard to justify. The woman replies that cheaper tickets exist.
explanation.es: El hombre dice que las entradas son tan caras que cuesta justificarlas. La mujer responde que hay entradas más baratas.

statements.text: Most cinemas may struggle to stay open in the long term.

explanation.en: The man wonders if cinemas will survive apart from blockbusters. The woman says she is more optimistic.
explanation.es: El hombre duda de que los cines sobrevivan salvo los de grandes estrenos. La mujer dice que es más optimista.

statements.text: Cinemas could attract audiences by offering more than just films.

explanation.en: The woman suggests live music or talks before the films. The man only says it would tempt him, without adding ideas of his own.
explanation.es: La mujer sugiere música en directo o charlas antes de las películas. El hombre solo dice que le tentaría, sin aportar ideas propias.
